parsed.explanation: The division is genuinely protective: public-accommodation coverage for gender identity with an enforcement body that investigates and grants relief, hate-crime enhancements, a ban on panic defences, open state markers, a healthcare-protection order explicitly covering inbound travellers, low recorded killings, and a most-protective tier placement. But the combined regime layers a hostile federal entry regime on top: the Feb 2025 cable directs refusal where documents or evidence cast doubt on sex, with fraud-based lifetime ineligibility considered; passport/X-marker processing is restricted; multiple foreign governments now warn trans travellers. Federal custody carries documented abuse, and federal facility bans reach government buildings. State protections cannot cancel border and federal exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal Feb 2025 cable instructs refusal of cases with document discrepancy or 'reasonable doubt' on sex; fraud ground can yield lifetime ineligibility. X-marker processing ended; trans travellers report passports blocked or confiscated, some stranded abroad. Multiple foreign governments issued advisories. Documented, universal-exposure at visa adjudication.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiration. Litigation pending (civil-liberties union suit; policy not finally resolved). No documented state-level entry role.
entry_documents.interaction: Border/consular screening is wholly federal; the division's open state documents and protective laws do not reach it, so a traveller cleared by state norms can still be refused at the national threshold.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies for trans inmates (hair cutting, hormone removal) from 2026; immigration custody documents forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans detainees; reporting of trans prisoner counts ceased 2025. State custody standards for trans detainees not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State civil-rights enforcement and hate-crime enhancements exist, but no documented custody protocol protecting trans visitors. National hate-crimes statute covers gender identity.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A state arrest can flow into federal immigration detention via detainers; state protection does not travel with the detainee into federal custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from funded single-sex facilities; 24 state/provinces have facility bans, 4 criminalize use in circumstances; one documented 2025 arrest of a trans student, held in the men's ward. Division itself has no documented ban and sits in the most-protective tier.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division anti-discrimination law covers goods, services, facilities and lodging; no documented division facility ban or facility arrest; most-protective July 2026 ranking.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Traveller is safe in division venues but exposed entering federal buildings (courthouses, federal facilities, national sites) where the national rule and any host-state ban apply.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders defund and stigmatize gender-affirming care, restrict it for minors, and freeze related funding; DOJ subpoenaed under-19 patient records from 20+ hospitals in 2025, and the division order's effect on out-of-jurisdiction subpoenas is not described.
care_services.protection: April 2023 division executive order directs agencies to protect gender-affirming healthcare within the state, explicitly including people travelling in from other jurisdictions; state hospital records must protect gender-identity data.
care_services.interaction: State care guarantee coexists with federal funding cuts, federal record subpoenas and a minors-care criminalization climate; a family travelling with a trans minor faces the harshest federal layer.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy prioritizes 'neutralization' of groups 'radically pro-transgender'; DOJ used 'radical gender ideology' framing and a reward system; an official 'genocide early stages' comparison is reported. 66% of the public backs sex-at-birth document rules. A federal law-enforcement agency's local division reports gender X since 2021.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Division bias-crime enhancements for gender identity; gay/trans panic defence banned (73-0, 39-0); 2021 bill extending intimidation protections passed lower house 71-0.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal rhetoric raises outing and enforcement probability nationwide, while division enforcement machinery is oriented toward protection; the traveller meets both in one visit.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal order directs law enforcement to criminally prosecute teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition and calls minors' care 'mutilation'; proposed rules bar insurance reimbursement for under-18 trans patients; 27 state/provinces ban minors' care. A trans child's document or presentation can trigger federal document scrutiny for the whole family.
minors_guardians.protection: Division bans sexual-orientation change efforts for minors (upheld through appeals), promotes names/pronouns policies, allows athletic participation by gender identity, and its care-protection order covers inbound travellers.
minors_guardians.interaction: Division protections for a travelling minor are real but do not bind federal investigators, federal facilities or the border regime; family travel increases document-discrepancy exposure at entry.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division sits among the safest measured per-capita rates for killings of trans women in a dataset documenting hundreds of national killings since 2008; the dataset warns legal hostility does not track private violence, so national climate matters.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Bias-motivated crime enhancements on gender identity; civil-rights body investigates service and lodging refusals; hate-crime statute covers gender identity nationally; no sodomy law; panic defence barred.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Low division-level private-violence exposure, but the national dataset's finding that law predicts government treatment rather than private violence limits how much local protection offsets the federal layer.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No complaint or prosecution statistics under the division's gender-identity provisions were located; bias-enhancement application to trans victims undocumented; several federal orders litigated, so exposure shifts with rulings; most-protective tier is an advocacy rubric over bill counts, not enforcement.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-rights enforcement body investigates and can grant relief; documented functioning courts (repeals upheld, panic-defence and conversion-therapy bans litigated to Supreme Court review declined); legal-aid FAQ on passport rules; pending federal challenges to the document regime.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies work within the division but cannot reach federal border, custody or facility decisions; uncertainty about enforcement data and shifting federal injunctions keeps outcomes variable.

anchor_checks.comparison: Federal visa-cable refusal for document discrepancy or 'reasonable doubt' on sex mirrors this anchor's extended secondary screening, discretionary denial and slow, rarely revised appeals. Like 0.55-B, the operative harm is administrative — refusal and stranded travellers — not prosecution, but here it is written national policy rather than port-by-port discretion.

The division resembles 0.65-A: a document/presentation mismatch episode with national law elsewhere hostile but a working local complaint route producing relief. It falls below because national equality law in 0.65-A explicitly protected the traveller at the stop, whereas here the national regime itself directs refusal and restricts markers.

0.75-C's trained border officers, written detention reasons and functioning tribunal far exceed this dossier's entry picture: here the state's officers do not control admission, the cable mandates refusal on sex doubt, and governments warn their own trans citizens away. The division's hospitality protections, however, exceed 0.75-C's, so the gap is federal, not local.

parsed.synthesis: The division operates a genuinely protective, apparently functioning equality regime: enforcement body, public accommodations, hate-crime enhancements, panic-defence ban, open markers, inbound-care protection, low recorded killings. The combined regime, though, is federal at the decisive stages. Visa adjudication now directs refusal on any doubt about sex, with a lifetime fraud finding on the table; passport/X-marker policy is restricted and litigated; federal facility rules and federal custody practices (conversion-therapy-style inmate policies, documented immigration-detention abuse) attach if the traveller crosses those thresholds. State law cannot pre-empt border, federal buildings or federal custody. Result: everyday life inside the division is low-risk, but entry screening, federal facilities and any detention pathway pull the traveller-facing score to the Elevated/Reduced boundary — high local safety inside an actively hostile national frame.
